---
title: "Estimate a hemodynamic response"
subtitle: "Fit smooth FIR curves and inspect their uncertainty."
jupyter: python3
---

{{< include ../_plot-setup.qmd >}}

A canonical HRF fixes the response shape before fitting. When the shape
itself is the question, `estimate_hrf` fits condition-level curves using a
smooth finite impulse response (FIR) basis. It returns an `HrfEstimate` with
response curves, standard errors, intervals, and the selected smoothing
penalty. This example uses simulated data so the fitted shape can be compared
with the generating HRF.

On a narrow screen, scroll plots horizontally to read their labels. Select a
plot to open a complete view.

## Simulate two condition responses

The event model generates an SPM canonical response for two alternating
conditions. Condition B has twice the amplitude of condition A in the first
feature. The second feature has a smaller response to both conditions.

```{python}
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
import fmrimod as fm

rng = np.random.default_rng(180)
events = pd.DataFrame({
    "onset": np.arange(8.0, 190.0, 10.0),
    "condition": np.resize(["A", "B"], 19),
    "duration": 0.0,
    "run": 1,
})
sampling = fm.SamplingFrame(blocklens=220, TR=1.0)
generating_model = fm.event_model(
    "onset ~ hrf(condition, basis='spmg1')",
    data=events, sampling_frame=sampling, durations=0.0, block="run",
)
amplitudes = np.array([[1.0, 0.7], [2.0, 1.4]])
signal = np.asarray(generating_model.design_matrix) @ amplitudes
response = signal + rng.normal(scale=0.04, size=signal.shape)
dataset = fm.fmri_dataset(response, tr=1.0, events=events)
```

## Fit the response shape

Formula-plus-dataset calls without a numeric basis select the smooth FIR
estimator. Here `k=8` sets eight free B-spline coefficients per curve, and
`lam="gcv"` chooses one smoothing penalty by generalized cross-validation
across the responses. The default baseline is a constant. The estimated
curves are constrained to zero at the start and end of the requested span.

```{python}
hrf_fit = fm.estimate_hrf(
    form="onset ~ hrf(condition)", dataset=dataset, block="run",
    rsam=np.arange(0.0, 21.0), k=8, lam="gcv", ci_level=0.95,
)
hrf_fit.curve_info
```

The estimate arrays are ordered as time × curve × feature. Use `curve_info`
to identify the curves and `time` for the post-stimulus grid.

```{python}
#| fig-width: 9
#| fig-height: 3.6
#| fig-alt: "Two panels comparing smooth FIR estimates for conditions A and B with the simulated SPM response in feature one. Shaded bands show model intervals. Condition B has twice the amplitude."
#| fig-cap: "Simulated data, feature 1. Solid curves are smooth FIR estimates; dashed curves are the generating HRFs. Shading shows 95% pointwise model intervals. These intervals do not account for model-selection uncertainty or unmodeled temporal correlation."
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.6), sharex=True, sharey=True)
truth_shape = np.asarray(fm.get_hrf("spmg1")(hrf_fit.time)).reshape(-1)
for curve, ax in enumerate(axes):
    color = ["#24786f", "#c26143"][curve]
    label = str(hrf_fit.curve_info.iloc[curve]["condition"])
    truth_row = 0 if label.endswith("A") else 1
    ax.plot(hrf_fit.time, hrf_fit.estimate[:, curve, 0], color=color, label="FIR estimate")
    ax.fill_between(hrf_fit.time, hrf_fit.lower[:, curve, 0],
                    hrf_fit.upper[:, curve, 0], color=color, alpha=0.18)
    ax.plot(hrf_fit.time, truth_shape * amplitudes[truth_row, 0],
            color="#526265", linestyle="--", linewidth=1.3, label="Generating HRF")
    ax.axhline(0, color="#aeb8b7", linewidth=0.7)
    ax.set_title(f"Condition {label.rsplit('.', 1)[-1]}")
    ax.set_xlabel("Time after event (s)")
axes[0].set_ylabel("Response amplitude")
axes[1].legend(loc="upper right")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

## Inspect the smoothing choice

The selected penalty and effective degrees of freedom describe the fitted
curve's flexibility. GCV chooses from the candidate grid; it does not prove
that the response model or residual assumptions are appropriate for a real
acquisition.

```{python}
pd.Series({
    "selected penalty": hrf_fit.lam,
    "effective degrees of freedom": hrf_fit.edf,
    "residual degrees of freedom": hrf_fit.df_residual,
    "curves": len(hrf_fit.curves),
    "features": len(hrf_fit.voxels),
})
```

For labeled output, use `hrf_fit.tidy()`. To evaluate the fitted curves on
another grid within the fitted span, use `hrf_fit.predict(...)`.
Matrix calls that supply `Y`, `X_trials`, and a numeric two-dimensional
`basis` use the older voxel-HRF compatibility estimator; they do not return
this smooth FIR result.
